themes.label: Functional mean-shift model and covariance eigenstructure
themes.need: Someone modeling a possible one-time mean shift in functional data needs the formal model (eq. 1.1), its distributional assumptions, and how the covariance operator's eigen-decomposition (Karhunen-Loeve/Mercer) is estimated under the null hypothesis of no change.

themes.label: Existing mean-shift test statistic and its limit theorem
themes.need: Someone wants the existing projection-based test statistic Sn,d (Berkes et al.) for testing whether a functional mean change exists at all, and its limiting null and alternative distributions (Theorem 1.1), before attempting to locate the change.

themes.label: Change-point location estimator and its HA setup
themes.need: Someone who has detected a functional mean change wants the location estimator k-hat_n* (eq. 2.1) and the supporting theory of how the covariance operator's eigenstructure behaves under the alternative (KA decomposition, Proposition 2.1, principal-component scores, the constant-vs-vanishing change-size regimes) needed to derive the estimator's asymptotics.

themes.label: Theorem 2.1: limit distribution for a constant-size change
themes.need: Someone wants the limit distribution of k-hat_n* when the functional mean change has a fixed (non-vanishing) size, together with its full proof: the shared criterion-decomposition machinery, the closeness (Op(1)) and weak-convergence lemmas, and the Appendix A verification lemmas the proof relies on.
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 2.1's proof (Section 4.2) reuses the shared E/D-term decomposition set up earlier in Section 4.1 and explicitly invokes Appendix A ('It is shown in the Appendix that this deterministic part is the dominating term') for its verification lemmas; a Figure 2 caption and navigation/caption trash interpose within the Section 4.1 preliminaries per document layout.

themes.label: Theorem 2.2: limit distribution for a vanishing-size change
themes.need: Someone wants the limit distribution of k-hat_n* when the functional mean change's size shrinks to zero as the sample grows (rate condition on Delta_n), together with its full proof: the closeness and weak-convergence lemmas under the vanishing-delta rate, and the Appendix B verification lemmas the proof relies on.
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 2.2's proof (Section 4.3) reuses the shared decomposition from Section 4.1 (soft-linked via t04) and explicitly invokes Appendix B ('It is shown in Appendix B that ... this deterministic part is the dominating contributor') for its verification lemmas.

themes.label: Consistency failure when the change is orthogonal to the leading eigenspace
themes.need: Someone relying on the change-point estimator wants to know the condition under which it FAILS to be consistent: when the mean-change function is orthogonal to the subspace spanned by the first d eigenfunctions used in estimation, and why simply using more components isn't the fix.

themes.label: Finite-sample validation of the constant-size-change theorem (Table 1)
themes.need: Someone wants empirical evidence (bias, RMSE, MAE across sample sizes n and true change locations tau*, for BM and BB processes) that the constant-size-change estimator behaves as Theorem 2.1 predicts.

themes.label: Finite-sample validation of the vanishing-size-change theorem (density plots)
